title: Safe Abstractions
concept: Wrap unsafe code in safe abstractions with contracts — exposing only a safe API while handling all the danger internally.
why: Unsafe code is inevitable (hardware access, FFI, performance). The art is containing it behind safe interfaces so callers can't misuse it.
tips: Keep unsafe blocks as SMALL as possible — the less unsafe code, the easier to audit
Every public method on a type containing unsafe data MUST have contracts
Never expose raw pointers in public APIs — wrap them
Test unsafe wrappers with fuzzing and sanitizers — trust but verify
common_mistakes: Exposing raw pointers in the public API — callers can bypass your safety checks
Forgetting that invariants protect the WRAPPER but not the underlying unsafe operation — both need checking
Writing too much unsafe code in one block — split into small, auditable pieces
